title: Meta's $18 billion teen-safety deal is about to hit earnings
detail:
Meta's $18 billion teen-safety deal is about to hit earnings
Tobi Opeyemi Amure, Robert Davey
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 7:37 AM MST 6 min read
META
^GSPC
Trade META on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

If you own an S&P 500 index fund, you own a slice of Meta Platforms. That means the company's next earnings report lands in your retirement account whether you follow the stock or not.

This one comes with an unusual line item. It's a bill for how Facebook and Instagram treated teenagers.

Meta Platforms (META) will release third-quarter results after the market closes on Oct. 21, the company said in a release. The company brought in about $201 billion in revenue in 2025, the Associated Press reported, which makes it one of the biggest earners inside the funds millions of Americans hold for retirement.

Wall Street has been warming to its artificial intelligence push. "Introducing Muse, the personal agent that understands your goals and works 24/7 to get things done for you," said CEO Mark Zuckerberg when Meta launched the Muse agent on Sept. 8.

However, the bill for Meta's past is arriving at the same moment as the bill for its future. Both will show up in the numbers you see on Oct. 21.

According to a Bank of America research report dated Oct. 16 and reviewed by TheStreet, Meta's third-quarter profit is likely to look far weaker than Wall Street expects, even as its ad business keeps growing at a healthy clip.

What Bank of America expects on Oct. 21

BofA expects revenue of $63.8 billion, ahead of the $63.3 billion consensus and near the top of Meta's own guidance range of $61 billion to $64 billion. That would mean roughly 25% growth from a year earlier.

Profit is a different story. BofA cut its third-quarter earnings estimate to $3.79 a share from $7.08, below the Street's $6.08, because it expects Meta to book a one-time $10 billion legal charge in the quarter.

More Artificial Intelligence:

Bank of America sees 40% upside in AI's next bottleneck

Micron stock faces unexpected trouble despite sold-out AI factory

Samsung's AI glasses make a bold bet against Meta

"We see upside potential to 3Q revenues given solid ad checks," wrote BofA analyst Justin Post in the note, titled "3Q Preview: Back on offense with AI." Post said his estimates sit above the Street, once the one-time charge is stripped out.

Here's what that means in plain terms. Earnings that would have come in near $7 for every share you own, now land closer to $4 for the quarter, almost entirely because of one legal bill.

The BofA research note points to several other numbers worth watching:

Instagram's global daily users rose six percent from a year earlier in the third quarter, while Facebook's fell eight percent, according to Sensor Tower data.

U.S. users spent an average of 58 minutes a day on Instagram in September, up 12%, versus 34 minutes on Facebook, down ten percent.

Muse passed 8.9 million downloads and 2.23 million daily active users, as of Oct. 12.

BofA expects Meta to guide fourth-quarter revenue to between $71.5 billion and $74.5 billion, up 19% to 24% from a year earlier.

Investor confidence in the companies driving the AI boom has taken a significant hit over the past week, with markets spooked by concerns that the revenues delivered by the technology will not match expectations.

Chip giant Nvidia, a vital cog in the sector, lost more than $350bn in market value this week alone. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Sector fell more than 11 per cent during the week, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 down 5.5 per cent.

In that context, Meta's earnings after the closing bell in New York on Wednesday offer a big test of Wall Street's mood about AI before Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon all report the following week.

The AI-led rally that has underpinned the stock market in recent years has been driven by bumper earnings from the major tech groups. However, "there is now a lot of anxiety, especially coming into the election period" before the US midterms next month, said Venu Krishna, head of US equity strategy at Barclays.

Although Meta's revenue is expected to have risen above $63bn in the third quarter, analysts estimate that the pace of growth will have slowed and the tech giant's adjusted operating income will be lower than in both the previous quarter and the third quarter of 2025 at $18.8bn. Operating margin is also expected to have tightened to a little under 30 per cent, as costs from the Facebook owner's AI investments bite, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

"Earnings are so critical, especially this quarter. The bar is very high. Last quarter we saw that companies that missed got punished a lot and companies that beat only got modest upside," Krishna added. "It's unlikely you'll have the same kind of returns [this quarter] you saw in the last three years." Ramsay Hodgson

How resilient is the Eurozone economy?

For the European Central Bank, the better than expected economic growth in the 21 countries that use the euro this year has been a mixed blessing.

The economy's surprising resilience in the face of surging energy costs, trade tensions and wider geopolitical uncertainty is positive for employment and strained public finances. However, with annual inflation at 3.8 per cent, almost twice the ECB's medium-term target of 2 per cent, stronger economic fundamentals may drive up inflation and could make an October interest rate rise more likely.

That is why next week's S&P Global Eurozone purchasing managers' indices — an important near-real-time gauge of economic activity — will be closely watched by analysts and traders. Economists polled by Reuters expect both the manufacturing and services indices to decline slightly to 52.5, comfortably above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction. This would represent a fall of 0.4 points in manufacturing and 0.5 points in services.

Earnings season picks up this week, with two Magnificent 7 members' results taking center stage.

Meta Platforms and Tesla will hand in their quarterly numbers on Wednesday, kicking off a series of reports from Big Tech. Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon are slated to join the fun next week, followed by Apple on Nov. 2. (Nvidia, the most valuable member of the group, won't report for some time.) The tech sector—and the seven biggest names in it—have played an outsize role in the stock market's recent gains.

Meta will address investors weeks after releasing a widely-embraced AI agent and tailoring the tool for businesses. The momentum comes after Meta's investment in AI weighed on its profits last quarter.

Investors are also watching Tesla's investments. The electric vehicle company missed earnings estimates last quarter as it spent heavily on autonomous vehicle and robot projects. Tesla's third-quarter EV deliveries came in ahead of estimates, and it last week showed off the Roadster, a sports car capable of dashing through the air. But Tesla is also facing a probe into the safety standards surrounding Cybercab, its driverless ridesharing service.

The results due in the week ahead may also offer insight on credit card spending and media streaming. Travel, too, with four airlines slated to report: Airline executives were optimistic this spring that consumers would pay higher airfare, but air travel was down about 5% year-over-year in September, and Delta Air Lines recently issued a softer-than-expected outlook.

Market Recap

The major indexes recorded mixed results for the week. The Dow industrials rose 0.7%, while the S&P 500 fell 2%. A tough week for tech shares weighed particularly on the Nasdaq, which retreated 4.5%, ending a four-week streak of wins. A hotter-than-expected inflation reading fueled speculation that the Fed will continue raising rates, while memory stocks fell after a Chinese firm said it had made an advancement in memory chip production. For more, read Friday's market recap here.

This Week's Top Events

Here's a list of major events happening this week. TradingView publishes a more detailed calendar, but clicking the link will take you off the Investopedia site.

Tuesday, Oct. 20: General Motors (GM) is slated to release its third-quarter results at 6:30 a.m., followed by a conference call at 8:30 a.m. GM wants to expand its defense business and recently announced a partnership with weapons manufacturer Lockheed Martin (LMT).

Tuesday: Netflix (NFLX) is set to publish its third-quarter results at 4:01 p.m. ET and host a live interview with executives at 4:45 p.m. ET. The streaming giant's second-quarter numbers were largely in line with expectations, but the company forecast that revenue growth would slow. The streamer announced layoffs last week. Spotify (SPOT) also reports this week.

Wednesday, Oct. 21: Lam Research Corp. (LRCX) is set to discuss its "September quarter" results on a conference call at 5 p.m. ET, with the numbers expected earlier in the afternoon. The company, which produces chipmaking equipment, has enjoyed strong demand during the AI buildout.

Wednesday: IBM (IBM) is scheduled to publish its third-quarter results and host a conference call at 5 p.m. ET. The software giant's stock plunged after it handed in disappointing preliminary results last quarter. IBM said clients were spending less on software and more on server and memory products, which have seen prices surge in recent months.

Wednesday: Meta Platforms (META) is slated to issue its third-quarter results after the stock market closes, followed by a conference call at 5:30 p.m. ET. The social media giant made a record amount of revenue in the second quarter, but earnings came up short of expectations, and shares slid.

Wednesday: Tesla (TSLA) is scheduled to report its third-quarter results after the closing bell, followed by a live question-and-answer webcast at 5:30 p.m. ET.

Thursday, Oct. 22: American Airlines (AAL) is scheduled to host a conference call on its third-quarter results at 8:30 a.m. ET, with the figures expected shortly before then. The airline beat estimates last quarter, but shares fell when it released a downbeat forecast. United Airlines (UAL), Alaska Air Group (ALK) and Southwest Airlines (LUV) also report this week.

Thursday: Procter & Gamble (PG) is slated to hold a conference call on its fiscal first-quarter results at 8:30 a.m. ET, with the numbers expected before then. The company behind Tide and Pampers missed revenue estimates last quarter, sending its stock downward.

Thursday: Comcast (CMCSA) is scheduled to release its third-quarter results and host a conference call at 8:30 a.m. ET. Company shares took off this summer when the internet and wireless provider announced plans to spin off its media arm, NBCUniversal. AT&T (T) also reports this week.

Thursday: Western Digital (WDC) is set to release its fiscal first-quarter results after the closing bell and hold a conference call at 4:30 p.m. ET. The memory and data storage company beat expectations last quarter. Toshiba's plans to double its hard-disk-drive capacity recently weighed on the sector.

title: President Trump Sells Micron Stock and Buys Another Mega-Cap Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock
detail:
President Trump Sells Micron Stock and Buys Another Mega-Cap Artificial Intelligence (AI) Stock
Trevor Jennewine, The Motley Fool
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 2:08 AM MST 5 min read
MU
META
NVDA

Trading disclosure

A financial disclosure from the Office of Government Ethics shows that President Trump's brokerage accounts executed over 500 trades in August. Those accounts are managed by third-party institutions, meaning Trump himself was not responsible for the decision to buy or sell any security.

However, the trades are still worth examining. In August, the president's accounts sold Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), with net sales totaling $251,000 to $515,000. Meanwhile, the largest buy was Meta Platforms (NASDAQ:META), with net purchases totaling $5.1 million to $25.3 million.

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Here's what investors should know about these artificial intelligence stocks.

President Donald J. Trump stands at a podium during a White House press briefing. Image source: Official White House Photo by Andrea Hanks.

Micron Technology: The stock President Trump's accounts sold in August

Micron manufactures memory and data storage solutions built on DRAM and NAND flash technology. CPUs store information on NAND (long-term memory) and use DRAM (working memory) to perform tasks. Also, GPUs use a specialized type of DRAM called high-bandwidth memory (HBM), which accelerates complex tasks like artificial intelligence by rapidly feeding data to processor cores.

Micron has benefited greatly from a critical supply shortage in memory chips fueled by the AI boom. However, the company ranks third in DRAM, HBM, and NAND market share after Samsung and SK Hynix, and it lacks a durable competitive advantage because memory chips are considered commodities, as wafers from different suppliers are interchangeable.

"We do not believe Micron has an economic moat," wrote William Kerwin at Morningstar. "We view DRAM and NAND as commodity-like products prone to market supply/demand dynamics and steady pricing erosion." However, Kerwin also thinks the AI boom will create a strong tailwind for the company in the medium term.

Micron reported strong financial results in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, which ended in September. Revenue increased 379% to $54 billion, driven by strong growth across every business segment. Non-GAAP net income soared to $33.42 per diluted share, an 11-fold increase from $3.03 per diluted share last year.

Micron should benefit as the AI build-out continues to drive demand for memory across GPUs, servers, and storage. Next year, the company expects volume production of its 512GB DDR5 DRAM server modules, which reduce operating power by 60% versus four 128GB modules. Micron also expects volume production of HBM4E, an enhanced version of the HBM4 memory it began shipping earlier this year.

What Advanced Micro Devices Buyers Were Betting On Before A 137% Rally

If you only skimmed the headlines about AMD's MI450 accelerators landing multi-gigawatt deals with Anthropic and Meta, the real surprise sat in the share chart. Holding Advanced Micro Devices from the start of the year would have returned 136.6%, including dividends. If you were deciding on 1 January 2026, before trillion dollar market caps and raised AI forecasts, what would you realistically have needed to believe about AMD's data center push to press "buy"?

The useful thing about a Narrative is that the reasoning is checkable: the assumptions sit beside the argument, and together they imply an estimated Fair Value you can disagree with.

Advanced Micro Devices has already moved. Pinpoint other ways to investigate the theme among 55 AI infrastructure stocks.

The Argument You Would Have Been Weighing Up On AMD

The shares cost US$214 at the start of the period. Anyone looking at Advanced Micro Devices then had to decide whether AI infrastructure could justify paying close to the bullish Fair Value of US$227, or whether that optimism had already gone too far.

The bullish story put Fair Value at US$227. It relied on AI driven data center demand, faster MI350 deployment, and a step up in revenue and margin expansion supported by advanced process nodes and full stack solutions.

The more cautious view landed on a Fair Value of US$185. It treated 20.3% revenue growth and a 17.8% profit margin as ambitious and focused on execution risk, tougher competition, and the strain from heavy AI and adaptive computing investment.

NasdaqGS:AMD Trailing 12-Month Earnings & Revenue History as at Oct 2026
What The AMD Evidence Actually Tested

AMD's Q2 2026 report did the heavy lifting for the bullish case. Revenue moved from US$7,685m in Q2 2025 to US$11,536m, while net income shifted from US$768m to US$2,305m and net margin went from 10.0% to 20.0%. That combination of higher sales and a higher margin supported the more optimistic narrative rather than the cautious one.

The key lesson is simple. When a story depends on both rapid top line expansion and richer profitability, you assess it by tracking revenue and net margin together instead of focusing only on the share chart.

What AMD's 137% Run Already Prices In

Advanced Micro Devices now trades at US$529, after a 136.6% gain from the start of the year. The selected Narrative's Fair Value sits below that level, treating the current quote as demanding rather than cheap.

The thesis leans on AMD's MI350 and future MI400 accelerators turning AI interest into lasting data center earnings. A buyer today effectively assumes that AI hardware ramps smoothly, so QuanD's execution and competitive risks become the pressure test for that belief.

Graph showing growth ©Adobe Stock Images

JPMorgan strategists expect third-quarter corporate earnings to provide support for equity markets, citing indications that profit growth is expanding beyond artificial intelligence-related companies and across a wider range of sectors.

A team led by Mislav Matejka said earnings expectations remain elevated at the index level but become more moderate when the contribution from individual companies is excluded. The strategists believe the reporting season could shift investor attention towards corporate fundamentals following recent market volatility.

US Earnings Forecasts Reflect Significant Contributions From Technology Companies

According to IBES consensus estimates, earnings per share for the S&P 500 are expected to increase 24% in the third quarter. Estimates from FactSet and LSEG indicate growth of 30%, reflecting an adjustment for a one-off tax charge at Meta (NASDAQ:META).

Excluding Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) and Micron Technology (NASDAQ:MU), expected earnings growth falls to 15%. The median S&P 500 company is projected to report an 8% increase.

In Europe, consensus forecasts indicate earnings growth of 19%, declining to 11% when energy companies are excluded. Median earnings growth is estimated at 9%, while median revenue growth stands at 7% for both the S&P 500 and the Stoxx 600.

JPMorgan said these figures suggest that earnings expectations are less demanding across the broader market than headline index forecasts indicate.

Economic Indicators Point to Continued Earnings Expansion

The bank identified improvements in global purchasing managers' indices during the third quarter, with several measures reaching multi-year highs.

JPMorgan's proprietary earnings indicator also continued to rise. According to the strategists, the indicator typically leads reported earnings by approximately two quarters, providing a basis for their expectations of continued growth over the next two reporting periods.

The team also reported that the proportion of global companies experiencing accelerating earnings growth is approaching a record level.

Although artificial intelligence remains a significant contributor to US corporate earnings, JPMorgan said profit growth is becoming more widely distributed across industries.

European Profit Margins and Sector Outlook

In Europe, JPMorgan expects operating margin expansion to contribute to earnings growth. The bank forecasts earnings before interest and taxes as a percentage of sales at 14.4% this year, approximately 250 basis points above the 2019 level.
